verified-feline-struvite-cystolith.credit: Bludwar · Public-domain dedication on Wikimedia Commons
verified-feline-struvite-cystolith.history: Wikimedia source identifies a feline struvite bladder stone; signalment and diagnostic confirmation method are not supplied.
verified-feline-struvite-cystolith.lookFor: Find the urinary bladder region; look for a mineral-opaque focus within its expected lumen. Ask whether location is confirmed on an orthogonal projection.
verified-feline-struvite-cystolith.quality: Original source does not establish the projection name. Confirm correct anatomical positioning and projection marker before interpreting.
verified-feline-struvite-cystolith.findings: Source-labeled mineral opacity compatible with a bladder calculus; verify the position relative to the expected urinary bladder and surrounding pelvis.
verified-feline-struvite-cystolith.interpretation: Source-reported feline cystolith, described by its author as struvite. Radiography alone is not sufficient to establish stone composition.
verified-feline-struvite-cystolith.differentials: Radiopaque urolith, mineralized soft tissue outside the bladder, or superimposed fecal/other mineral opacity; localization from orthogonal images is important.
verified-feline-struvite-cystolith.why: Calcium-containing and some magnesium-ammonium-phosphate calculi can be radiopaque. Opacity, shape and position inform the workup but do not confirm chemistry.
verified-feline-struvite-cystolith.next: Urinalysis, urine culture when indicated, imaging in another plane, and composition analysis where available.

verified-canine-cystolith-overview.quality: The source does not specify projection or diagnostic technique, and this is a photograph of a displayed radiograph.
verified-canine-cystolith-overview.findings: Original photographer identifies urinary bladder stones. Describe number, size, mineral opacity and location rather than assuming composition.
verified-canine-cystolith-overview.interpretation: Source-identified canine cystoliths; size/composition should not be inferred without further examination.
verified-canine-cystolith-overview.differentials: Bladder calculi versus extravesical mineral opacity or superposition. Consider possible urethral urolithiasis if clinical obstruction is suspected.

verified-canine-cystolith-overview.next: Combine with urinalysis, culture when indicated and urinary ultrasound or complementary projections; evaluate urinary outflow urgently if obstructed.

images.caption: Source annotation labels CE, HL, SD, DB, and PA radiographic measurement concepts.

verified-equine-laminitis-radiographic-m.history: Original creator presents annotated measurements relevant to assessing laminitis; individual patient signalment is not specified.
verified-equine-laminitis-radiographic-m.lookFor: Find P3, the dorsal hoof wall, the solar surface and the coronary band. What each line measures is more important than memorizing a value from this single image.
verified-equine-laminitis-radiographic-m.quality: Annotated educational reference, not an independent clinical measurement from a supplied case history.
verified-equine-laminitis-radiographic-m.findings: CE = coronary extensor distance; HL = horn–lamellar distance; SD = sole depth; DB = digital breakover; PA = palmar angle, per original figure description.
verified-equine-laminitis-radiographic-m.interpretation: Radiographic measurement teaching guide for monitoring structural effects of laminitis. Annotations do not alone establish individual severity.
verified-equine-laminitis-radiographic-m.differentials: Differentiate hoof capsule conformation and positioning effects from actual distal phalanx displacement using standardized technique and clinical context.
verified-equine-laminitis-radiographic-m.why: Loss of integrity of the suspensory lamellae can permit displacement of P3, alter sole depth and change the relationship between dorsal hoof wall and bone.
verified-equine-laminitis-radiographic-m.next: Use standardized marker placement and consistent limb positioning; compare serial radiographs with veterinary and farrier findings.

verified-canine-medial-patellar-luxation.history: Uploader identifies a Bichon Frisé with bilateral medial patellar luxation; no additional clinical history supplied.
verified-canine-medial-patellar-luxation.lookFor: Identify left and right using the L marker. Locate each patella relative to its femoral trochlea; check for asymmetry. Also review the cranial field for incidental findings.
verified-canine-medial-patellar-luxation.quality: VD view includes pelvis and pelvic limbs. Note alignment/rotation and whether patellar position is affected by stance.
verified-canine-medial-patellar-luxation.findings: Source: left patella (right side of image; L marker) medial to trochlea, grade 3; contralateral grade 2; small incidental urinary bladder calculi in upper right field.
verified-canine-medial-patellar-luxation.interpretation: Source-identified bilateral medial patellar luxation. Grading involves physical examination; source states left grade 3 and right grade 2.

verified-canine-medial-patellar-luxation.next: Correlate with orthopedic exam and clinical lameness; evaluate incidental cystoliths if clinically indicated.

verified-canine-distal-femur-osteosarcom.title: Canine Distal Femur · Aggressive Osteolysis (Osteosarcoma Source Case)

images.caption: Original uploader identifies substantial bone destruction in distal femur of dog with osteosarcoma.

verified-canine-distal-femur-osteosarcom.history: Source identifies a dog with distal femoral osteosarcoma. Independent pathology and complete signalment are not supplied.
verified-canine-distal-femur-osteosarcom.lookFor: Identify distal femoral cortex and medullary bone. Locate the destructive radiolucent zone; describe margins, transition zone, cortical integrity and any adjacent reaction.
verified-canine-distal-femur-osteosarcom.quality: Photograph of radiograph (3,072 × 2,304 pixel file). Use for recognizing prominent lysis rather than assessing fine detail or precise measurements.
verified-canine-distal-femur-osteosarcom.findings: Original uploader describes a large dark region in distal femur representing bone destroyed by the tumor. Characterize this radiographically as focal aggressive-appearing osteolysis.
verified-canine-distal-femur-osteosarcom.interpretation: Uploader-described canine distal femoral osteosarcoma. Radiography alone cannot distinguish all aggressive neoplasms from osteomyelitis.
verified-canine-distal-femur-osteosarcom.differentials: Primary bone neoplasia (including osteosarcoma), osteomyelitis, other aggressive bone processes.
verified-canine-distal-femur-osteosarcom.why: Osteolysis represents net loss of mineralized bone. Rapid tumor-driven destruction can obscure normal trabecular/cortical boundaries and increase pathologic fracture risk.
verified-canine-distal-femur-osteosarcom.next: Obtain appropriately positioned orthogonal views and clinical staging; consider tissue diagnosis with specialist consultation.

verified-canine-bilateral-hip-dysplasia.title: Canine Pelvis · Bilateral Hip Dysplasia in Young Labrador

images.caption: Source reports bilateral hip dysplasia in Labrador puppy; left side has particularly poor femoral head coverage.

verified-canine-bilateral-hip-dysplasia.history: Labrador Retriever puppy; original description reports bilateral hip dysplasia with left worse than right.
verified-canine-bilateral-hip-dysplasia.lookFor: Compare femoral head coverage by acetabula, joint congruity and symmetry. Confirm marker/laterality: the dog's left side appears on image right, per source.
verified-canine-bilateral-hip-dysplasia.quality: Photograph of film; use for gross joint coverage, not formal hip scoring or submillimeter measurement.
verified-canine-bilateral-hip-dysplasia.findings: Source identifies reduced acetabular coverage of both femoral heads, particularly on the left; evaluate joint subluxation.
verified-canine-bilateral-hip-dysplasia.interpretation: Original-source described bilateral canine hip dysplasia.
verified-canine-bilateral-hip-dysplasia.differentials: Developmental hip dysplasia versus projection-induced apparent asymmetry or traumatic instability; history and positioning matter.
verified-canine-bilateral-hip-dysplasia.why: Insufficient congruity and laxity shift loading across cartilage/subchondral bone and predispose to secondary osteoarthritis.
verified-canine-bilateral-hip-dysplasia.next: Clinical orthopedic evaluation and standardized hip studies when indicated; do not assign formal scoring from an informal film photograph.

studyImageReview.note: Photo of radiograph. Anatomic changes source-described; not suitable for formal hip scoring.

verified-feline-pleural-effusion-fip.title: Feline Thorax · Pleural Effusion (FIP-Labeled Teaching Radiograph)

images.caption: Source annotations indicate dependent pleural fluid obscuring cardiac borders, with relatively little aerated lung.

verified-feline-pleural-effusion-fip.history: Original image is labeled as a cat with FIP. Confirmatory diagnostic workup is not provided.
verified-feline-pleural-effusion-fip.lookFor: Locate dependent soft-tissue/fluid opacity, effacement of the cardiac silhouette and remaining aerated dorsal lung. Consider what compartment contains the fluid.
verified-feline-pleural-effusion-fip.quality: Small annotated image (1,020 × 501 pixels). Best for pleural-fluid recognition, not small pulmonary lesions.
verified-feline-pleural-effusion-fip.findings: Source annotation describes dependent thoracic fluid, loss of visible cardiac margins and compressed/limited aerated lung.
verified-feline-pleural-effusion-fip.interpretation: Pleural effusion pattern. FIP is the source-attributed disease, not a diagnosis established by this radiograph alone.
verified-feline-pleural-effusion-fip.differentials: FIP-associated effusion, cardiac disease, pyothorax, chylothorax, neoplasia, hemorrhage and other causes of pleural effusion.
verified-feline-pleural-effusion-fip.why: Fluid in the pleural space contrasts poorly with heart/soft tissue and restricts lung expansion; the lung retracts from chest wall and border effacement occurs.
verified-feline-pleural-effusion-fip.next: If dyspneic, stabilize first and consider oxygen and ultrasound-guided thoracocentesis where indicated; evaluate effusion and underlying cause.

studyImageReview.note: Low-resolution pre-annotated image; best used as broad pleural-effusion pattern reference.

verified-feline-right-pulmonary-opacity-.title: Feline Thorax · Asymmetric Pulmonary Opacity and Suspected Neoplasia
verified-feline-right-pulmonary-opacity-.lecture: Small Animal Thorax · Pulmonary patterns and differential diagnosis

images.caption: Source reports diffuse right-lung increased opacity and a left bronchoalveolar pattern. Subsequent CT reportedly suggested malignant neoplastic disease.

verified-feline-right-pulmonary-opacity-.history: 12-year-old male European cat; source describes subsequent deterioration and CT suspicious for malignant neoplastic disease with possible renal metastasis.
verified-feline-right-pulmonary-opacity-.lookFor: Confirm the DV projection and compare pulmonary opacity right versus left. Describe distribution and silhouette border changes before naming disease.
verified-feline-right-pulmonary-opacity-.quality: Full original 1,915 × 2,392 JPEG published by creator. Technical diagnostic quality and interpretation not independently verified.
verified-feline-right-pulmonary-opacity-.findings: Source describes diffuse increased opacity over right lung except craniomedial part of right cranial lobe, left bronchoalveolar change and cardiac border effacement.
verified-feline-right-pulmonary-opacity-.interpretation: Marked asymmetric pulmonary opacity. Source reports follow-up CT highly suspicious for malignant neoplasia; histopathologic confirmation not supplied.
verified-feline-right-pulmonary-opacity-.differentials: Pulmonary neoplasia, pneumonia, edema, hemorrhage, atelectasis or combined disease processes depending on clinical context.
verified-feline-right-pulmonary-opacity-.why: Replacement of aerated lung by cells, exudate, fluid or mass tissue increases radiographic opacity. Pattern and distribution narrow but do not uniquely identify etiology.
verified-feline-right-pulmonary-opacity-.next: Correlate with respiratory stability; consider orthogonal images and CT or sampling when appropriate.

studyImageReview.note: Source full-size digital image available; original radiologic findings reported by uploader; do not claim confirmed histology.

verified-feline-pregnancy-fetal-skeleton.title: Feline Abdomen · Mineralized Fetal Skeletons

images.caption: Source identifies five fetal skeletons in gravid queen; count only distinctly visible skulls/spines.

verified-feline-pregnancy-fetal-skeleton.history: Source describes queen approximately one and a half months pregnant and five similarly sized fetuses.
verified-feline-pregnancy-fetal-skeleton.lookFor: Identify mineralized fetal skulls and vertebral columns; distinguish overlapped skeletons before estimating fetal count.
verified-feline-pregnancy-fetal-skeleton.quality: Original 1,554 × 2,321 JPEG, source annotated on Commons. Cannot judge fetal viability from this static radiograph.
verified-feline-pregnancy-fetal-skeleton.findings: Multiple mineralized fetal skeletons within maternal abdomen; original creator describes five fetuses.
verified-feline-pregnancy-fetal-skeleton.interpretation: Radiographic evidence of pregnancy. Fetal count is source-reported, not independently verified from every visible skeleton.
verified-feline-pregnancy-fetal-skeleton.differentials: No alternate etiology needed when multiple fetal skeletal structures are established; distinguish count uncertainty due to overlap.
verified-feline-pregnancy-fetal-skeleton.why: Fetal skeletal mineralization produces visible radiopaque skulls, spines and limbs later in gestation. Radiography does not establish fetal heart rate or viability.
verified-feline-pregnancy-fetal-skeleton.next: Use clinical examination and ultrasound for fetal viability when clinically indicated.

exam1-canine-paraprostatic-cyst-ultrasou.history: Canine ultrasound example with source-identified paraprostatic cyst; signalment unspecified.
exam1-canine-paraprostatic-cyst-ultrasou.lookFor: Identify the cystic fluid region relative to soft tissue. Evaluate the role of anechoic lumen, wall boundaries, and possible distal enhancement.
exam1-canine-paraprostatic-cyst-ultrasou.quality: Very low-resolution, annotated ultrasound. Use for recognizing a cystic versus solid region, not quantification.
exam1-canine-paraprostatic-cyst-ultrasou.findings: Original source labels a cyst adjacent to the prostate. A fluid-filled structure typically has few internal echoes.
exam1-canine-paraprostatic-cyst-ultrasou.interpretation: Source-defined paraprostatic cyst; this frame alone cannot establish complete etiology or anatomy.
exam1-canine-paraprostatic-cyst-ultrasou.differentials: Fluid-filled cyst vs other cystic pelvic structures; prostate pathology may coexist.
exam1-canine-paraprostatic-cyst-ultrasou.why: Uniform fluid gives few returning echoes and may produce increased brightness immediately deep to the fluid because sound attenuation is low.
exam1-canine-paraprostatic-cyst-ultrasou.next: Compare with full ultrasound series and clinical context.

verified-feline-abdomen-foreign-body-shr.title: Feline Abdomen · Metallic Shrapnel Localization Reference

images.view: Cat abdomen · source projection not specified
images.caption: Real Siamese cat abdominal radiograph taken to follow a fragment of shrapnel in the left side; source metadata mentions previously sustained projectile injuries.

verified-feline-abdomen-foreign-body-shr.history: Four-year-old Siamese cat with an embedded shrapnel fragment in left side. The examination was intended to evaluate the fragment.
verified-feline-abdomen-foreign-body-shr.lookFor: Orient the film, identify radiopaque metallic material and localize it in projection relative to abdominal tissues without claiming a specific organ location from a single view.
verified-feline-abdomen-foreign-body-shr.quality: Original 1350 × 1692 JPEG; source metadata notes image orientation rotation; must verify display against anatomy.
verified-feline-abdomen-foreign-body-shr.findings: Radiopaque foreign material is source-described. Location relative to internal structures requires orthogonal projections.
verified-feline-abdomen-foreign-body-shr.interpretation: Source-identified retained shrapnel, not a GI obstruction or intestinal foreign body.
verified-feline-abdomen-foreign-body-shr.differentials: External metallic artifact, implant or retained projectile material; localization requires context.
verified-feline-abdomen-foreign-body-shr.why: Metal attenuates radiographs more strongly than mineral or soft tissues, producing marked radiopacity.
verified-feline-abdomen-foreign-body-shr.next: Check projection/marker, compare orthogonal images if available, and assess whether further localization changes management.

verified-canine-gdv-bloat-film.history: German Shepherd with gastric dilation and volvulus; source describes GDV.

verified-canine-gdv-bloat-film.quality: 2592 × 1944 photograph of an X-ray. Source does not provide acquisition metadata or definitive projection label.
verified-canine-gdv-bloat-film.findings: Marked gastric gaseous dilation on source-confirmed GDV radiograph.
verified-canine-gdv-bloat-film.interpretation: GDV is source-attributed; avoid treating a large stomach alone as proof of volvulus.
verified-canine-gdv-bloat-film.differentials: Food bloat, gastric outflow obstruction, functional gastric ileus, aerophagia.
verified-canine-gdv-bloat-film.why: Gastric volvulus twists the stomach, trapping gas and compromising vascular return.
verified-canine-gdv-bloat-film.next: Emergency stabilization and veterinary surgical assessment.

exam2-case1-dsh.title: Exam 2 · Abdomen Cases · Abdomen case 1 · effusion, mixed intestinal gas and mass effect
exam2-case1-dsh.history: 10-year-old DSH cat. Anorexia; no other information provided.
exam2-case1-dsh.lookFor:
Describe serosal detail before choosing the most defensible differentials.
Work systematically: views and positioning, then each organ system (liver, spleen, stomach, small intestine, colon, kidneys, bladder), serosal and retroperitoneal detail, then Roentgen signs before naming a diagnosis.
exam2-case1-dsh.findings: Professor's notes: two views. Loss of serosal detail in the abdomen with a fluid-filled appearance (ascites). Increased radiolucency in the stomach, small intestine and colon; small-intestinal gas distension with multiple populations; greater gas distension in the fundus. Mass effect with leftward displacement. Small mineral/radiopaque material that appears to be bone in the intestines; some fecal material in the rectum and colon. If there were a perforation you would also expect free gas.
exam2-case1-dsh.interpretation: Differentials discussed in class: ruptured mass (neoplasia), hemoabdomen, foreign-body perforation, ascites (e.g., right-sided heart failure), distended bladder. Radiographs alone do not give the final diagnosis.

exam2-case3-dmh-hairties.title: Exam 2 · Abdomen Cases · Abdomen case 3 · equivocal intestinal pattern
exam2-case3-dmh-hairties.history: 2-year-old DMH cat. History of eating hair ties; anorexia, lethargy.
exam2-case3-dmh-hairties.lookFor:
List each objective sign and explain why the imaging remains indeterminate. Rank functional ileus versus possible early/partial obstruction and choose appropriate next diagnostics.
Work systematically: views and positioning, then each organ system (liver, spleen, stomach, small intestine, colon, kidneys, bladder), serosal and retroperitoneal detail, then Roentgen signs before naming a diagnosis.
exam2-case3-dmh-hairties.findings: Professor's notes: abnormal arrangement of the small intestine ("tortuous turns", "stacking"). Mixed populations of intestinal diameter. Colon enlarged with fecal material (constipation). The border of the spleen is not clearly seen.
exam2-case3-dmh-hairties.interpretation: Equivocal. Rule-outs: constipation, foreign body, and ileus (functional or mechanical); the radiologist stated either. Plan discussed in class: enema, then repeat radiographs (the enema will introduce some gas). Decide on surgery from the clinical signs (GI signs, litter box); if the cat has not defecated within 1–2 hours, exploratory surgery is better than not, but be transparent with the owner about cost.

exam2-gi-minpin-linear.title: Exam 2 · GI Principles · GI patient · intestinal gas shapes (Min Pin)
exam2-gi-minpin-linear.lecture: CVM 743 · Exam 2 · Gastrointestinal Principles I & II
exam2-gi-minpin-linear.history: 1-year-old FS Miniature Pinscher. Vomiting since yesterday, straining to defecate this morning.
exam2-gi-minpin-linear.lookFor:
Identify plication-related signs and reasonable next steps.
Work systematically: views and positioning, then each organ system (liver, spleen, stomach, small intestine, colon, kidneys, bladder), serosal and retroperitoneal detail, then Roentgen signs before naming a diagnosis.

exam4-l8-fred.title: Exam 4 · L8 Putting it all together · Fred · 10 yr MC DSH
exam4-l8-fred.lecture: CVM 743 · Exam 4 · L8 · Thorax: Putting It All Together
exam4-l8-fred.history: 10-year-old MC DSH cat. Two months of decreased appetite that improved with a stimulant. Grade II/VI parasternal systolic murmur. 1) Describe the abnormalities. 2) Radiographic diagnosis? 3) What next?
exam4-l8-fred.lookFor: Work systematically: technique and positioning, then heart, lungs (pattern + distribution), vessels, pleura, mediastinum, trachea, esophagus, ribs/sternum and the edges of the film. Commit to ONE primary differential.
exam4-l8-fred.findings: Slide answer: increased soft-tissue opacity in the pleural space allowing retraction of the lung lobes from the periphery. Professor's notes: primary conclusion = pleural effusion! We can't see the heart, so we cannot state cardiomegaly. Can't rule out a mass; does have a heart murmur.
exam4-l8-fred.interpretation: Slide answer: pleural effusion (differentials: heart failure, malignancy, transudate, chyle, exudate). Professor's notes: acquired cardiomyopathy leading to congestive heart failure; hyperthyroid; could be a cranial mediastinal mass too. Next: thoracocentesis + repeat radiographs (horizontal-beam view). Slide plan/outcome: thoracocentesis and re-radiograph, echocardiogram → malignant effusion with mixed inflammation, mild concentric LV hypertrophy, masses with pleural effusion seen on echo ("effusion due to cancer + heart").
exam4-l8-fred.source: L8_Thorax_putting_it_all_together__282_29.pdf · slide 14 · LMU CVM 743 course material, used with LMU permission (non-commercial)
exam4-l8-fred.credit: Dr. Lynn Griffin, DVM MS DACVR DACVR(RO) · LMU CVM 743

exam4-l8-maeby.findings: Professor's notes: angular opacity in the esophagus (marked dorsal to the trachea/heart base); "radio is relative low"; heart measured.
exam4-l8-maeby.interpretation: Professor's notes: with esophageal rupture you will see pneumomediastinum. So do a barium(!) — could use iodinated contrast since that won't cause a reaction. (L7 slide: barium swallows are contraindicated if esophageal rupture is suspected.)
exam4-l8-maeby.source: L8_Thorax_putting_it_all_together__282_29.pdf · slide 35 · LMU CVM 743 course material, used with LMU permission (non-commercial)

exam4-lung-14yo-cat.title: Exam 4 · L1 Pulmonary patterns · 14 yr FS DSH · intermittent respiratory distress
exam4-lung-14yo-cat.lecture: CVM 743 · Exam 4 · L1 · Principles of Thoracic Evaluation & Pulmonary Patterns
exam4-lung-14yo-cat.lookFor: Work systematically: technique and positioning, then heart, lungs (pattern + distribution), vessels, pleura, mediastinum, trachea, esophagus, ribs/sternum and the edges of the film. Commit to ONE primary differential.
exam4-lung-14yo-cat.findings: Professor's notes: collapsed lung lobe — triangular, soft-tissue opacity; collapsed bronchus/lung lobe due to bronchial plugging, most common in the right middle lung lobe (cough ↑, surfactant ↓). Lungs hyperinflated! — because it's not ever fully expelling air → hyperexpanded. Shows "tenting" of the diaphragm; diaphragm pushed back/flattened. Mineralization could still be there with treatment, but less inflamed.
exam4-lung-14yo-cat.interpretation: Slide: radiographic consequences of bronchial disease (with chronic allergic bronchitis): lobar collapse (mucus plug, R middle most common, usually alveolar), bronchiectasis, spontaneous rib fx (9th–13th), hyperinflation (flattened/tented diaphragm), bronchial mineralization.
exam4-lung-14yo-cat.source: dc4b2e17-L1PulmonaryPatterns.pdf · slide 69 · LMU CVM 743 course material, used with LMU permission (non-commercial)

exam4-hrt-lchf-veins.title: Exam 4 · L4–5 Cardiac · Failure film · L4–5 slide 45
exam4-hrt-lchf-veins.lecture: CVM 743 · Exam 4 · L4–5 · Have a Heart: Cardiac Radiology
exam4-hrt-lchf-veins.lookFor: Work systematically: technique and positioning, then heart, lungs (pattern + distribution), vessels, pleura, mediastinum, trachea, esophagus, ribs/sternum and the edges of the film. Commit to ONE primary differential.
exam4-hrt-lchf-veins.findings: Slide: left-sided failure — pulmonary vessels are a window on cardiac function: pulmonary venous congestion (vein dilated, larger than the corresponding artery) is often the first sign of decompensation. Professor's notes: veins; LA enlargement; diameter of veins > arteries = venous congestion. A dog presenting for cough with lungs sounding a bit harsh and a left-sided heart murmur = not exactly in congestive failure, but almost there.

exam4-hrt-cocker.title: Exam 4 · L4–5 Cardiac · 9 yr MC Cocker Spaniel mix
exam4-hrt-cocker.lecture: CVM 743 · Exam 4 · L4–5 · Have a Heart: Cardiac Radiology
exam4-hrt-cocker.history: 9-year-old MC Cocker Spaniel mix. Coughing, exercise intolerance.
exam4-hrt-cocker.lookFor: Work systematically: technique and positioning, then heart, lungs (pattern + distribution), vessels, pleura, mediastinum, trachea, esophagus, ribs/sternum and the edges of the film. Commit to ONE primary differential.
exam4-hrt-cocker.findings: Professor's notes: interstitial coalescing to alveolar pattern (see bronchograms), which is most severe in the caudodorsal perihilar region. L cardiomegaly and LA enlargement — "what is it that's big on this dog?" LV + LA enlargement; trachea starting to run parallel. Then look at blood vessels in the cranial and dorsal aspect: smaller lumen diameter of arteries, pretty symmetric; veins are ventral + central; bigger = venous congestion.
exam4-hrt-cocker.interpretation: Slide report: L cardiomegaly and LA enlargement with interstitial to alveolar pattern primarily in the caudodorsal lung field, L>R; mild venous congestion. Diagnosis: cardiogenic edema secondary to left-sided congestive heart failure.

exam4-hrt-cat-edema.title: Exam 4 · L4–5 Cardiac · Feline film · L4–5 slides 65 & 70
exam4-hrt-cat-edema.lecture: CVM 743 · Exam 4 · L4–5 · Have a Heart: Cardiac Radiology

exam4-hrt-cat-edema.findings: Professor's notes: always ask first: abnormal or normal? Possible alveolar; struggling to see the heart because of the pulmonary pattern; a bit of a diffuse unstructured interstitial pattern. Instead of venous congestion, cats get vascular congestion — can be either arteries, veins, or both.
exam4-hrt-cat-edema.interpretation: Slide: cardiogenic pulmonary edema in a cat. No typical pattern of cardiogenic edema in cats — often more patchy; can also have pleural effusion with left-sided heart failure; look for cardiac changes! Professor's notes: how to see what everything is → does the heart look big? If yes → Lasix trial.

exam4-hrt-arthur.title: Exam 4 · L4–5 Cardiac · Arthur · 5 mo MI Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier
exam4-hrt-arthur.lecture: CVM 743 · Exam 4 · L4–5 · Have a Heart: Cardiac Radiology
exam4-hrt-arthur.history: "Arthur", 5-month-old MI Soft Coated Wheaten Terrier. Presented for dyspnea. VI/VI holosystolic murmur.
exam4-hrt-arthur.lookFor: Work systematically: technique and positioning, then heart, lungs (pattern + distribution), vessels, pleura, mediastinum, trachea, esophagus, ribs/sternum and the edges of the film. Commit to ONE primary differential.
exam4-hrt-arthur.findings: Slide findings: generalized cardiomegaly (lateral 4–5 ICS wide, VD > 2/3 of the thorax); bulge at the caudodorsal heart margin and double opacity over the heart on VD (enlarged LA); elevation of the trachea over the heart; focal bulge of the descending aorta on VD; possible superimposed bulge at 1:00 (MPA enlargement); distension of the cranial lobar artery and vein (lateral) and caudal arteries and veins (VD); interstitial to alveolar infiltrates in the perihilar region and caudally. Professor's notes: abnormal! Heart too big → left side; arteries and veins circled.
exam4-hrt-arthur.interpretation: Slide diagnosis: PDA — heart changes and evidence of vascular overcirculation (VSD unlikely due to bulges in the aorta and possible MPA); congestive heart failure (perihilar interstitial to alveolar infiltrates); recommend echocardiography. Professor's notes: Wheaten terriers are also predisposed; recent dyspnea = going into congestive heart failure. Outcome: echo confirmed PDA, treated with successful coil embolization.
exam4-hrt-arthur.source: 18a9a98a-L42C5HaveaHeartCardiacRadiologyPartI.pdf · slide 136 · LMU CVM 743 course material, used with LMU permission (non-commercial)

exam4-cav-zoey.title: Exam 4 · L6 Thoracic cavity · "Zoey" · 11 yr FS mixed breed
exam4-cav-zoey.lecture: CVM 743 · Exam 4 · L6 · The (Rest of the) Thoracic Cavity, Part 1
exam4-cav-zoey.history: "Zoey", 11-year-old FS mixed-breed dog. LSA (lymphoma) patient, last staged clean 6 weeks ago; now slightly labored breathing, lethargic, big peripheral lymph nodes.
exam4-cav-zoey.lookFor: Work systematically: technique and positioning, then heart, lungs (pattern + distribution), vessels, pleura, mediastinum, trachea, esophagus, ribs/sternum and the edges of the film. Commit to ONE primary differential.
exam4-cav-zoey.findings: Slide: radiographs before and after thoracocentesis ("post-tap"), including horizontal-beam views. Lecture: pleural effusion is a clinical sign, not a diagnosis — use thoracocentesis and recheck films, and a horizontal beam to move fluid away from the area of interest.
exam4-cav-zoey.interpretation: Pleural effusion (repeat after thoracocentesis to look at what the fluid was hiding).

exam4-cav-cat-caudal.title: Exam 4 · L6 Thoracic cavity · 7 yr FS cat · fever, vomiting
exam4-cav-cat-caudal.lecture: CVM 743 · Exam 4 · L6 · The (Rest of the) Thoracic Cavity, Part 1
exam4-cav-cat-caudal.lookFor: Work systematically: technique and positioning, then heart, lungs (pattern + distribution), vessels, pleura, mediastinum, trachea, esophagus, ribs/sternum and the edges of the film. Commit to ONE primary differential.
exam4-cav-cat-caudal.findings: Slide: the follow-up slide outlines a triangular soft-tissue opacity in the caudal mediastinum (dorsal, between heart and diaphragm) on the lateral and on fluoroscopy.
exam4-cav-cat-caudal.interpretation: Slide: caudal mediastinal mass effect — less common than cranial/middle; most often due to esophageal disease (megaesophagus, esophageal tumors, foreign bodies), abscesses, atypical LN enlargement, mediastinitis (secondary to esophageal perforation). Dilemmas: pleural fluid trapped in the plica vena cava, diaphragmatic masses; clinical signs and ancillary imaging help.

exam4-cav-beagle.findings: Slide: follow-up slide arrows: ventral deviation of the carina on the lateral; widening/opacity at the hilus on the VD. exam4-case3-dachshund.title: Exam 4 · L7 Thoracic cavity · Case 3 · 8 yr MC Dachshund
exam4-case3-dachshund.lecture: CVM 743 · Exam 4 · L7 · The (Rest of the) Thoracic Cavity, Part 2
exam4-case3-dachshund.lookFor: Work systematically: technique and positioning, then heart, lungs (pattern + distribution), vessels, pleura, mediastinum, trachea, esophagus, ribs/sternum and the edges of the film. Commit to ONE primary differential.
exam4-case3-dachshund.findings: Case notes: generalized cardiomegaly (VHS 13.2, 4 ICS); bulge at the caudal cardiac waist on the L lat view; pulmonary vasculature normal; diffuse interstitial to alveolar pattern, worse caudodorsally.

exam4-case4-blue.title: Exam 4 · L7 Thoracic cavity · Case 4 · "Blue", 8 yr MC mixed breed
exam4-case4-blue.lecture: CVM 743 · Exam 4 · L7 · The (Rest of the) Thoracic Cavity, Part 2
exam4-case4-blue.history: "Blue", 8-year-old MC mixed-breed dog. Gagging for 8 weeks; lame for 2 weeks after a fall.
exam4-case4-blue.lookFor: Work systematically: technique and positioning, then heart, lungs (pattern + distribution), vessels, pleura, mediastinum, trachea, esophagus, ribs/sternum and the edges of the film. Commit to ONE primary differential.
exam4-case4-blue.findings: Case notes: increased soft-tissue opacity (mass) in the cranial thorax, on the right and left on the VD; dorsal and rightward deviation of the trachea; mediastinal shift to the right; multiple round soft-tissue nodules in the lungs.
exam4-case4-blue.interpretation: Case notes: cranial mediastinal mass and pulmonary nodules — R/O ectopic thyroid carcinoma, thymic tumor, MH, LSA (less likely).

exam4-case6-golden.title: Exam 4 · L7 Thoracic cavity · Case 6 · 4 yr MC Golden Retriever
exam4-case6-golden.lecture: CVM 743 · Exam 4 · L7 · The (Rest of the) Thoracic Cavity, Part 2
exam4-case6-golden.history: 4-year-old MC Golden Retriever. Returned home with a 2-inch bleeding laceration in the region of the thoracic inlet; decreased dorsal lung sounds on the right; lame on the right forelimb.
exam4-case6-golden.lookFor: Work systematically: technique and positioning, then heart, lungs (pattern + distribution), vessels, pleura, mediastinum, trachea, esophagus, ribs/sternum and the edges of the film. Commit to ONE primary differential.
exam4-case6-golden.findings: Case notes: increased visualization of structures of the cranial mediastinum, vessels and esophagus; gas pocket ventral to the cardiac silhouette on the lateral with mild elevation of the heart off the sternum; mild diffuse interstitial pattern; gas in the soft tissues of the right body wall and axilla. Professor's notes: SQ gas; gas in the mediastinum; heart elevated/gas under heart.
exam4-case6-golden.interpretation: Case notes: SQ emphysema, pneumomediastinum and pneumothorax (mild), likely due to a penetrating wound.

exam4-case7-hwd.title: Exam 4 · L6 Thoracic cavity · Case 7 · 4 yr mixed breed
exam4-case7-hwd.lecture: CVM 743 · Exam 4 · L6 · The (Rest of the) Thoracic Cavity, Part 1
exam4-case7-hwd.lookFor: Work systematically: technique and positioning, then heart, lungs (pattern + distribution), vessels, pleura, mediastinum, trachea, esophagus, ribs/sternum and the edges of the film. Commit to ONE primary differential.
exam4-case7-hwd.findings: Slide findings: convex right heart with increased sternal contact; prominent bulge in the region of the main pulmonary artery; enlarged, tortuous pulmonary arteries throughout the lung fields; mild bronchointerstitial pattern in the caudal lung lobes.
exam4-case7-hwd.interpretation: Slide conclusion: heartworm disease with probable pneumonitis — right heart enlargement + pulmonary artery enlargement + mild parenchymal changes is classic in endemic regions. Next step: heartworm antigen test (CT not necessary for initial diagnosis).

exam4-case9-mainecoon.title: Exam 4 · L7 Thoracic cavity · Case 9 · 4 yr MC Maine Coon
exam4-case9-mainecoon.lecture: CVM 743 · Exam 4 · L7 · The (Rest of the) Thoracic Cavity, Part 2
exam4-case9-mainecoon.lookFor: Work systematically: technique and positioning, then heart, lungs (pattern + distribution), vessels, pleura, mediastinum, trachea, esophagus, ribs/sternum and the edges of the film. Commit to ONE primary differential.
exam4-case9-mainecoon.findings: Case notes: generalized cardiomegaly (VHS 9.5; "valentine" outline on VD); left atrial / bi-atrial enlargement; interstitial to alveolar pattern, diffuse, worse ventrally (alveolar AND bronchial on the close-up); equivocal pulmonary vessel enlargement (veins; right caudal artery and vein).
exam4-case9-mainecoon.interpretation: Case notes: cardiomegaly — cardiomyopathy (HCM, DCM, other), valvular disease, hyperthyroidism; pulmonary edema from L-CHF; pneumonia much less likely. Pre- vs post-diuretic VD shown.
